critical_code_review_comments: seed.py upsert_user now correctly gates password self-heal behind SEED_DEMO=='true' (line 27). The fix is minimal and correct. Consider logging when the demo self-heal fires so a future accidental prod SEED_DEMO=true is easier to detect.
seed.py reads os.environ['SEED_DEMO'] directly which raises KeyError if unset; harmless in prod (var is set) but a `.get('SEED_DEMO','false')` would be safer.
Consider suppressing the recharts width/height warnings by giving chart containers explicit minHeight; not blocking.

context_for_next_testing_agent: Bug fix for silent password reset on backend restart is verified. Test script /app/backend/tests/test_seed_no_reset.py sets its own env and can be re-run standalone with `python /app/backend/tests/test_seed_no_reset.py`. Preview and production login both healthy. Do not brute force production (5 fail = 15min lock).
rca of the issue: seed.upsert_user unconditionally re-hashed and overwrote the admin's password_hash whenever the stored hash didn't verify against ADMIN_PASSWORD from .env. On production (SEED_DEMO=false) this meant every backend restart reverted a user's freshly-changed admin password back to the .env value, eventually causing 5 failed logins -> 15 min lockout. Fix: gate the reset behind `elif os.environ['SEED_DEMO']=='true' and not verify_password(...)`, so production restarts leave existing password_hash untouched while demo self-heal still works. Verified in isolated DB: after user changes hash to NewPass456!, running seed() with SEED_DEMO=false preserves NewPass456!; with SEED_DEMO=true it resets back to ADMIN_PASSWORD as expected.
